Priscilla Chan founded a school in 2016; 10 yrs later, it closed after $125m funding The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. SpaceX rocket debris crashes into Moon, blasts 60-foot crater Unexpectedly, a four-ton SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket stage has collided with the Moon, exhibiting the increasing issue of space debris. After spending over a year in orbit, the remnants triggered observable spectral lines indicative of sodium and lithium gases upon impact. NASA, alongside South Korea, intends to photograph the resulting crater to understand the event better. This incident underscores the urgency of addressing space junk management and its proper disposal.

Chubby marmots join subscription service after sanctuary faces money trouble In a creative twist, a biologist from Colorado turned to popular subscription service to secure funding for crucial marmot research. He shares engaging and family-oriented videos featuring yellow-bellied marmots, motivated by recent federal budget cuts affecting his long-standing project. Operating for over sixty years, this initiative not only raises awareness about marmot populations but has also begun to generate essential financial support for ongoing scientific investigations.

After 'ban' on Claude Code, Microsoft has more 'bad news' for Anthropic Microsoft has told engineers that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for" in a new internal memo from EVP Jay Parikh. The memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default internal model, replacing an auto-router that had been sending GitHub Copilot workloads to Anthropic's Claude. Every Microsoft division now carries an AI token budget target, months after Claude Code licences were cancelled.

Trump administration refunds $100 billion in tariffs struck down by US Supreme Court In a significant move, the Trump administration has reimbursed nearly one hundred billion dollars in tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled against wide-ranging duties. By July, around sixty percent of these tariffs were refunded to importers. The court's decision emphasized that the existing law did not provide blanket authority for imposing tariffs. Moving forward, Trump is leveraging alternative legal channels to impose new tariffs.

Neil Armstrong's boyhood home built in 1908 hits market for $430,000 For sale is the childhood home of Neil Armstrong in Wapakoneta, Ohio, a historic two-storey residence that has been lovingly preserved for nearly forty years. This house boasts many original features that tie it to the first man on the Moon, making it a site of interest for history buffs and space enthusiasts alike. The current owner hopes the new buyer will continue to honor its significant legacy.
